title: Orientation To Environmental Horticulture
description: Survey of the many facets and component sciences of environmental horticulture. Exploration of the multitude of career options available in the green industry. An introduction to the vocabulary of the environmental sciences, including the terminology used in the identification of plants. Foundations of plant science, such as plant structure, plant growth, and the environmental needs of plants.
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of career opportunities in the green industry through written examinations.
Demonstrate knowledge of the environmental horticulture sciences, including plant terminology, on written examinations.
objectives: Demonstrate knowledge of the horticultural industry and career opportunities in the green industry
Demonstrate knowledge of the environmental horticulture sciences, including plant terminology, structure, and nomenclature
Demonstrate the safe and proper handling of tools and use of structures used in the production of horticultural crops
Explain horticultural production concepts, such as media mixes, plant propagation, plant fertilization, and cultural practices
Identify common horticultural and interior plant pests and pest damage
Identify common turfgrass species and turfgrass cultural practices
Use floral practices to create a design
Exhibit an understanding of the significance of environmental horticulture for different cultures from around the world
content: The horticulture industry and green industry career opportunities
Variety of sciences which comprise or impact environmental horticulture
Workplace diversity in the green industry
Green industry markets locally and in California
Career opportunities in the green industry
Parks, recreation, and golf course management
Role of higher plants in the living world
Nomenclature, classification, and terminology used in plant identification
Origin, domestication, and improvement of cultivated plants
Use and management of horticultural tools and equipment
Plant sexual and asexual propagation techniques
Plant fertilization needs and fertilization techniques
Use of horticulture for food production
